title: Echo and Horizon
premise: Petra Kavanagh discovers that the shared dream infecting the colony's children is a distress signal from the cryosleep backups in his own cargo hold — ten thousand colonists from a destroyed sister ship, stored as living minds by the corporation that abandoned them. The colony's ruling council wants the backups erased to protect scarce resources; Petra's estranged daughter, now a council aide, wants them woken. As corporate enforcers arrive to purge the hold, Petra must choose between loyalty to the colony that took him in and the truth that survival bought with erasure is no survival at all. In the end he wakes the children's dreamers first — the youngest backups — sacrificing his navigator's license and freedom, but giving both halves of humanity a future stitched together.
about_author: Yara Sandoval is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. She lives in Valparaíso, where she writes stories about people who keep big machines — and bigger secrets — running.

chapters.title: The Hold Below
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. During a routine haul through contested orbits, Petra logs an anomaly in the sealed cargo hold: power draws consistent with active cryopods, not frozen freight. He tells himself it's nothing. Emotional beat: quiet dread — a man who has learned not to look too closely at what pays him.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Night
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Petra and Mirei Okonkwo, a colony schoolteacher. Children across the settlement begin describing one identical dream — a corridor of blue light and a voice counting down. Mirei reports it; the council dismisses it as mass hysteria. Beat: unease spreading like weather.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. He decrypts his own shipping manifest and finds the truth: the hold carries 10,000 minds from the wrecked colony ship Meridian, declared lost seven years ago — the same year he started this route. Beat: vertigo of complicity; he has been their jailer and never knew.

chapters.title: The Council's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Council POV via Petra's daughter, Ana Kavanagh, a junior aide. She learns the council has known for months and plans to vent the hold once the next supply contract signs. Father and daughter clash over dinner — their first real conversation in years. Beat: loyalty beginning to fracture along family lines.

chapters.title: What the Dream Wants
chapters.summary: Mirei's POV. A child leads her to the docking ring and recites Petra's ship registry number — information no one on the colony should have. Mirei confronts Petra; together they confirm the dreams are the backups broadcasting through the colony's network. Beat: reluctant alliance, awe edged with fear.

chapters.title: Enforcers at the Gate
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The corporation's purge team arrives early, citing 'cargo irregularities.' Petra stalls with forged telemetry while Ana steals the council's evidence cache. The countdown in the children's dream accelerates. Beat: the clock becomes the antagonist; paranoia tightens.

chapters.title: Ana's Choice
chapters.summary: Ana's POV. Cornered between her career, her council mentors, and her father's cause, she leaks the Meridian passenger list publicly. The colony splits — half demand justice, half fear the resource cost. Beat: costly courage; she burns her old life to tell the truth.

chapters.title: Venting Sequence
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, climax part one. Enforcers breach the hold to purge it. Petra flies manual evasive patterns no autopilot can match, buying minutes while Mirei and the children — still dreaming — guide him to the pods' manual release. Beat: white-knuckle action fused with the eerie intimacy of being steered by sleeping voices.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Climax. Power allows waking only a fraction of the backups. Petra chooses the children first — including a boy who has been dreaming of him by name. The enforcers stand down as colony crowds surround the dock, making erasure politically impossible. Beat: sacrifice crystallized; mercy as strategy.

chapters.title: Echo and Horizon
chapters.summary: Resolution, rotating POVs. Months later: the colony absorbs the awakened families; Petra, stripped of his license, teaches navigation to Meridian's orphans. Ana rebuilds the council from inside. The last dream fades — replaced by ordinary ones. Beat: bittersweet belonging; survival redefined as what we refuse to erase.
